title: When the Safehouse Turns
premise: Rosalind Villalobos, a peace-delegation interpreter who has survived three years of shifting rules by staying invisible, receives a meeting invitation from her handler, Marcus, two days after his confirmed death. Following it pulls her into a conspiracy inside the delegation itself: the peace talks are cover for a financial operation timed to Frankfurt's market open, and the defector she is ordered to extract, analyst Teodor Brandt, is both the key witness and the intended bait to flush out everyone who knows too much. Rosalind must choose between loyalty to the institution that trained her and the truth Marcus died protecting, aided reluctantly by delegation security officer Anselm Reyes, whose duty-bound worldview cracks as they uncover the rot together. In the end, Rosalind gets Brandt to Frankfurt not by extraction but by exposure—broadcasting the evidence during the talks' final session—and walks away from the service with Anselm, alive but permanently unmade, having traded invisibility for a truth that costs them everything else.
about_author: Ivo Halloran is the pen name of a former conference interpreter turned novelist who spent a decade in multilateral negotiations before trading the booth for the page. They write thrillers about people whose professional silence becomes unbearable.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Establishes her life interpreting for a failing peace delegation in Geneva: precise, rule-bound, deliberately unremarkable. She renders a hostile exchange between delegations into something almost civil, then goes home alone. Emotional beat: competent loneliness; the reader feels how much of herself she has edited out.

chapters.title: Two Days After
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At a memorial briefing for handler Marcus Ede, killed in an apparent car accident, Rosalind's secure terminal pings: a meeting invitation from Marcus's account, timestamped tomorrow, 06:00, location included. She reports it per protocol and is told to ignore it. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion.

chapters.title: Protocol Says No
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She spends the day testing the invitation against every rule she knows, and every rule says walk away. A colleague, Anselm Reyes, notices her distraction and covers for her during a tense session without knowing why. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture between obedience and instinct.

POV Rosalind. She goes anyway. The meeting point is a boathouse on the Rhône where she finds no Marcus—only a dead-drop phone preloaded with a partial file: the delegation's 'reconciliation fund' routes through shell accounts tied to Frankfurt positions opening Monday. Emotional beat: vertigo; the rules were never protecting her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Losses
chapters.summary: POV Teodor Brandt. Introduces the defector: a quantitative analyst who built the fund's models and has been quietly copying evidence, hiding inside the delegation's logistics office. He knows someone will come for him soon—he just doesn't know which side they'll be on. Emotional beat: paranoid patience.

chapters.title: Anselm's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Anselm Reyes. Security officer Anselm runs a routine audit and finds access anomalies around Brandt's office and, disturbingly, around Marcus's old files. His loyalty to the institution is absolute; he files a report and requests guidance. Emotional beat: faith in the system, about to be tested.

chapters.title: What the Booth Hears
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Interpreting a closed session, Rosalind hears a phrase from the dead-drop file spoken verbatim by a senior delegate—a sentence that should not exist outside the conspiracy. She realizes the talks themselves are choreography for the market play. Emotional beat: horror disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Deciphering Marcus's partial file, she finds her own name annotated in his handwriting: 'if anything happens, R.V. was never read in.' She understands he meant it as protection—and that it now marks her. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Crossing Reports
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Anselm's audit report triggers a visit from a 'liaison' who thanks him warmly and reassigns him off the delegation. The smoothness of it terrifies him more than any threat would. He begins pulling threads quietly instead. Emotional beat: disillusionment arriving like cold water.

chapters.title: The Extraction Order
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A new handler arrives with clean credentials and orders: extract Brandt before Sunday night, deliver him to a safehouse outside Basel. The order is authentic—which is exactly what makes Rosalind suspicious, because authenticity can be manufactured by whoever holds the system. Emotional beat: trust under interrogation.

chapters.title: Coffee with a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind and Anselm. Their investigations collide; each suspects the other until a grudging, wordless exchange of evidence over bad coffee. Anselm shows her the reassignment paper trail; she shows him the dead-drop file. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals choosing cautious alliance.

chapters.title: Brandt Runs
chapters.summary: POV Teodor. Spooked by a maintenance sweep of his office, Brandt bolts early with half his evidence, triggering the very manhunt he feared. His flight wrecks Rosalind and Anselm's careful timeline—the extraction window collapses to hours. Emotional beat: panic compressing everything.

chapters.title: Basel After Midnight
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind intercepts Brandt at a freight yard before the hunters do and delivers him to the safehouse—but finds signs it's already compromised: fresh cigarette ends, a camera angled wrong. The safehouse isn't shelter; it's a trap being set. Emotional beat: the ground tilting.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Turns
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. The ambush comes at dawn. Anselm, arriving to verify the site, walks into it and chooses sides in real time, helping Rosalind and Brandt fight out. They escape wounded, leaving behind the fiction that any of them still belong to the institution. Emotional beat: the point of no return, paid in blood.

chapters.title: Reading the Dead Handler
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Hidden in Brandt's copied data, they find Marcus's true last transmission: he'd discovered the operation and was silenced; the invitation was his failsafe, scheduled posthumously. Rosalind finally understands she wasn't recruited—she was trusted. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Forty Hours to Open
chapters.summary: POV Teodor. Brandt explains the mechanism: at Monday's Frankfurt open, coordinated trades will monetize the talks' engineered collapse unless his full dataset—keys, timestamps, account maps—is made public or delivered to regulators. The clock is now explicit. Emotional beat: clarity as fuel.

chapters.title: Every Exit Priced
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. The trio plans three exits—regulators, press, the plenary floor itself—and watches each get closed one by one as the conspiracy tightens its grip, culminating in a betrayal by the one colleague Anselm still believed in. Emotional beat: siege mentality; love and duty stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Offered reinstatement and immunity if she surrenders Brandt, Rosalind gives her answer in the only language she trusts: she interprets the offer aloud, precisely, so Brandt hears every word of what she's refusing. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed; loyalty redefined as truth-telling.

chapters.title: Final Session
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. During the closing plenary, Rosalind uses her interpreter access to hijack the floor's audio feed, reading the evidence live while Anselm holds the door and Brandt feeds her the sequence. Delegates freeze; markets begin to move early. Emotional beat: climax—silence broken at last.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens
chapters.summary: POV Teodor. The trades unravel publicly; positions collapse; arrests ripple outward as regulators act on the broadcast data. Brandt, no longer bait but witness, surrenders voluntarily to prosecutors. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: After the Feed Cuts
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Fallout: inquiries, scapegoating, a few honest convictions. Anselm testifies despite pressure, ending his career in the institution he loved, and finds he doesn't regret it. He and Rosalind acknowledge what they've become to each other without naming it yet. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning.

chapters.title: Unwritten Rules
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Months later, Rosalind works freelance interpretation far from Geneva, anonymous again but by choice this time. A postcard arrives with no signature—just a time and a place, in Marcus's old shorthand. She smiles, packs light, and decides on her own terms whether to go. Emotional beat: resolution with an open door.
